topIssues.title: Alert on proving progress failures or stalls
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body: If generating proofs fails or stalls when generating a proof we should be alerted. For example if `OPSuccinctDataFetcher` fails when fetching boot info. This is probably regular metrics reporting from the proposer and a grafana rule that alerts if the metrics aren't reported.

topIssues.title: op-revm: make the deposit gas-cap exemption a property of OpHandler::tx_gas
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Found while reviewing the reth v2.5.2 bump (#22495).

Deposits are exempt from the EIP-7825 transaction gas cap. Today that exemption is implemented only in `alloy_op_evm::OpEvm::transact_raw`, which temporarily replaces `cfg.tx_gas_limit_cap` with `u64::MAX` around a deposit ([`lib.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/lib.rs#L363-L376)). `OpHandler` itself does not override the gas split: revm 42 moved `initial_gas_and_reservoir` into a new defaulted `Handler::tx_gas` (`revm-handler` 42.0.1, `handler.rs:215`), called from `run_without_catch_error`, `run_system_call`, `runtime_oog_result` and the inspector path. A consumer driving published `op-revm` directly (`ExecuteEvm::transact`/`replay`/`transact_commit`) therefore hands an oversized deposit `cap - intrinsic` regular gas and parks the rest in the EIP-8037 reservoir, i.e. a spuriously OOG deposit. `op-revm` is a published crate; Flashbots' `op-rbuilder` redirects it to this repo via `[patch.crates-io]`.

Proposed: override `Handler::tx_gas` in `OpHandler` to pass `u64::MAX` for `DEPOSIT_TRANSACTION_TYPE` (next to the existing deposit skip in `validate_env`, [`handler.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs#L89)), then delete the save/restore in alloy-op-evm. The two deposit-cap tests in `alloy-op-evm/src/tests.rs` should keep passing unchanged, plus a new op-revm-level test.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: kona-node: optimism_outputAtBlock returns Internal error instead of not found for unknown blocks
topIssues.author: FlashWayne
topIssues.body:
Asking kona-node for `optimism_outputAtBlock` on a block it doesn't have yet returns `-32603 Internal error` instead of a "not found" error.

The engine query drops its response channel when `l2_block_by_label` returns `None` ([query.rs#L86-L88](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/query.rs#L86-L88)), and the RPC side turns any closed channel into `ErrorCode::InternalError` ([engine_rpc_client.rs#L68-L71](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/rpc/engine_rpc_client.rs#L68-L71)). So "block doesn't exist" looks the same as a real internal failure.

This matters for op-dispute-mon. The output agreement enricher only treats an RPC error containing "not found" as a missing block ([output_agreement_enricher.go#L97-L105](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/op-dispute-mon/mon/extract/output_agreement_enricher.go#L97-L105)), which is what op-node returns. With kona-node behind the rollup RPC, a game that claims a block beyond the node's head is counted as a node error. If every endpoint is kona, the game fails enrichment ("all nodes returned errors") instead of being flagged as a disagreement.

I'll open a PR that reports a missing block as a "not found" server error.

topIssues.title: kona-node: --l1.trust-rpc can't be turned off from the CLI and only header hashes are checked
topIssues.author: 0xShadowX
topIssues.body:
Two problems with how kona-node checks what the L1 RPC returns.

`--l1.trust-rpc` and `--l2.trust-rpc` default to `true` ([providers.rs#L8-L25](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/engine/providers.rs#L8-L25)) and are plain clap bool flags, so they can't be turned off from the command line. `--l1.trust-rpc=false` fails with `unexpected value 'false' for '--l1-trust-rpc' found; no more were expected`, and only `KONA_NODE_L1_TRUST_RPC=false` works. The help text says "If false, block hash verification is performed", but a CLI user can never get there.

Even with verification on, [`AlloyChainProvider`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/crates/providers/providers-alloy/src/chain_provider.rs#L83-L105) only compares the header hash with the requested hash. The transactions returned by `block_info_and_transactions_by_hash` are not checked against `transactions_root`, and `receipts_by_hash` never looks at `receipts_root`. An RPC that serves the right header but drops or changes batcher transactions, or deposit and config logs, gets through.

For comparison, op-node defaults `--l1.trustrpc` to false. When it doesn't trust the RPC it checks the block hash and the transactions root (`RPCBlock.Verify`), and it always checks receipts against the receipts root (`validateReceipts`).

I'll open a PR that makes both flags accept `=false` and adds the transactions and receipts root checks when the RPC isn't trusted. Whether the L1 default should flip to false like op-node is probably your call, so the PR leaves the default alone.

topIssues.title: kona-node: --l2.engine-timeout, --p2p.no-discovery and --p2p.peers.lo/hi/grace are parsed but never applied
topIssues.author: Bruce039
topIssues.body:
Same kind of problem as #22667. These kona-node flags are parsed into the CLI structs, but nothing reads them afterwards:

- `--l2.engine-timeout` / `--l2.timeout` (`KONA_NODE_L2_ENGINE_TIMEOUT`, default 30000 ms), [providers.rs#L67-L74](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/engine/providers.rs#L67-L74). The engine client is built in [`OpEngineClient::rpc_client`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/client.rs#L153-L161) from a plain hyper client with no timeout, and the engine tasks don't wrap the calls either. If the EL hangs on `engine_newPayload` or `engine_forkchoiceUpdated`, the engine actor just waits. op-node applies `--l2.engine-rpc-timeout` to every engine call.
- `--p2p.no-discovery` (`KONA_NODE_P2P_NO_DISCOVERY`), [p2p.rs#L60-L62](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/p2p.rs#L60-L62). [`NetworkDriver::start`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/crates/node/service/src/actors/network/driver.rs#L79) always starts discv5, so the node binds the discovery socket and publishes its ENR even when discovery is turned off, which is usually why a sequencer sets it.
- `--p2p.peers.lo`, `--p2p.peers.hi`, `--p2p.peers.grace`, [p2p.rs#L101-L117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5315305/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/p2p.rs#L101-L117). lo and hi only show up as labels in the CLI metrics. The gossip swarm has no connection limit, and every ENR discovery hands over gets dialed. op-node feeds these into its connection manager.

`grep -rn 'l2_engine_timeout\|no_discovery\|peers_grace' rust/kona` only finds the flag definitions and their parse tests.

I have a patch for the three and will open a PR.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: consolidate SDM checks in check-lagoon
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Lagoon currently requires separate tools and pre-funded senders to exercise Interop and SDM together. `check-lagoon all` now takes one funded account, deterministically derives and tops up a separate SDM sender on both chains, then concurrently runs the complete Interop smoke suite and policy-producing SDM workloads on both chains; focused `sdm` subcommands remain available for generated or existing-block checks. Legacy nonzero PostExec `gasPrice` responses remain compatible, and `sdm-devnet` remains temporarily for existing Kupcake wrappers.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22988

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: recover resolution and bonds beyond the observation window
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Games outside the 14-day observation window can still block resolution of tracked descendants. This PR extends resolution and bond recovery to their required ancestors without adding those ancestors to the proposal DAG.

Recovery scope:

- Normal bond recovery continues for games in `state.games`, including resolved entries.
- Only unresolved tracked games initiate parent traversal.
- Unresolved ancestors are followed and resolved parent-first, regardless of age.
- The first resolved ancestor is included for its own credit recovery, then traversal stops—even if older ancestors have outstanding bonds.
- Ancestor candidates are rebuilt each sweep, not retained independently. Recovery can stop before a withdrawal matures if the connecting child or intermediate ancestor resolves, or the child leaves the tracked set.
- No factory-wide historical bond scan, including after restart.

Existing policy and claim safeguards:

- Prestate-based eligibility remains unchanged, including for foreign-created games.
- Defense/proving policy is unchanged.
- Claims respect each game’s own registry, normal/refund distribution rules, finality, and withdrawal delay.
- Paused tracked games retain recovery eligibility; failed claim preflight reads defer submission.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18429

topPRs.title: all: log through op-service/log instead of go-ethereum/log
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Every Go file in the monorepo now logs through `op-service/log`, and a depguard rule (`geth-log` in `.golangci.yaml`) fails lint on any new `go-ethereum/log` import outside `op-service/log/logger.go`. This means the logger can later be swapped for an owned implementation in one place, which is what the op-geth cutover needs.

Behaviour does not change. The `op-service/log` names are type aliases of the go-ethereum ones, so this is a pure rename.

Import convention:
- A file that imported geth log unaliased now imports `op-service/log` unaliased as `log`, so only its import line changes.
- The former `gethlog` files (op-supernode, one op-conductor test) use `oplog`.
- A file that imported both packages now uses `log` for both.
- Files that never imported geth log keep their existing alias.

Stacked on #23013. Review and merge it after that PR.

Part of #22752.

topPRs.title: op-challenger: delete withdrawal proofs invalidated by challenger wins
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Adrian Sutton** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BTT5DGHA4/p1787791642391549?thread_ts=1787791642.391549&cid=C0BTT5DGHA4)_

Stacks on #22669.

**Before:** #22669 makes `deleteProvenWithdrawal` permissionless once the game a withdrawal was proven against resolves as `CHALLENGER_WINS`, but nothing calls it. Those proofs can never finalize, yet they stay in `provenWithdrawals` and keep counting toward `numProofSubmitters`, so anything reading the portal still sees a live proof against an invalid game.

**After:** op-challenger deletes them automatically. The feature is off unless `--optimism-portal-address` is set; when it is, the challenger logs once at startup and clears invalidated proofs on every L1 head, alongside bond claiming.

**How:** A new `game/withdrawals` scheduler runs beside the bond claimer and gets the same games list. For each game that resolved `CHALLENGER_WINS` it filters `WithdrawalProvenExtension1` logs from the game's `l1Head` block, batch-reads `provenWithdrawals` for the pairs it finds, and sends a delete for each one still recorded against that game. Deleted rows read back with a zero timestamp, which makes this idempotent; an in-memory per-game cursor keeps later heads to the new blocks only.

**For reviewers:** anyone can prove many cheap withdrawals against a game the challenger will win, making the challenger pay unrewarded gas to delete them all — hence off unless the portal address is set, and capped at 100 deletes per game per head. Unit tests only, no e2e or action-test coverage.

---

topPRs.title: rust: update reth to v2.6.0
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Moves op-reth onto the reth v2.6.0 dependency stack so it remains aligned with current reth, REVM, and Alloy APIs. The previous fork-only fixes are preserved or superseded upstream, and the Rust/security and reth-update reviews found no unresolved issues.

Migration notes: no flags are removed. `--engine.persistence-threshold` now defaults to 50 instead of 7, `--engine.num-state-masking-blocks` is new and defaults to 30, `--rpc-cache.max-cached-tx-hashes` now defaults to 100000 instead of 30000, and `--rpc-cache.max-headers` is now a hidden no-op; new controls are also available for HTTP compression, inline JWT secrets, and BAL caching.

Verified with the Rust workspace checks, feature combinations, mirror audit, and the affected CL sync, EL sync, and restart acceptance scenarios using both op-node and kona-node.
